chunks: And that which was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Al-'Is ibn Al-Qasim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who performed Umrah in Rajab, he said: 'If he stays in Mecca until he departs from it as a Hajj pilgrim, then a sacrifice (Hady) becomes obligatory upon him. But if he departs from Mecca before entering the state of Ihram from another place, then there is no sacrifice upon him.' This is applicable to one who stayed in Mecca and then performed Tamattu' (Umrah followed by Hajj) in the months of Hajj, because it is among what is recommended and encouraged. That which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.تَمَتَّع: Performed Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break)
key_terms.رَجَب: Rajab (a month in the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.يُحْرِم: Enters the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on offering a sacrifice for Umrah performed in Rajab if the person stays in Mecca for Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the obligation of the Hady sacrifice for those performing Tamattu' al-Hajj, specifically noting that remaining in Mecca after Umrah until Hajj Ihram triggers the sacrifice. The text contextualizes this within the recommended practice of performing Umrah in Rajab, linking the legal obligation to the spiritual merit of combining these pilgrimages during the sacred months. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the sacrifice is tied to the specific ritual structure of Tamattu' rather than the mere act of Umrah itself.
